lawyer:
Md Sagir Hossain, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Hasan Tareq, Advocate—For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Abdus Sobhan ------ Petitioner
vs
Md Abul Hossain and another ---- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
In this revision Rule was issued granting leave to revision at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 20-2-2018 passed by the learned District Judge, Barguna, in Civil Revision No. 32 of 2017 allowing the revision and reversing the judgment and order dated 1-6-2017 passed by  the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Patharghata, Barguna in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 allowing the application for staying all further proceedings of Title Execution Suit No. 04 of 2016 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the petitioner along with 19 others, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Patharghata, Barguna, against the opposite party No. 1 along with others for a declaration in the following manner: “ক) আরজির নিম্ন (খ) তপসিল বর্ণিত ভূমি সম্পর্কে (ক) তপসিল বর্ণিত বিরোধীয় রায় ও ডিক্রি ভাক্ত, যোগাযোগী, ফেরবী, অকার্যকরী, অকর্মন্য, শঠতামি, তঞ্চকলা মূলক মর্মে রদ ও রহিতের ডিক্রি দিবার ।”

3. In the plaint the plaintiffs amongst other stated that opposite party No. 1, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 2011 against the petitioner and others, as defendant, for a decree of partition and in the said suit no summons were duly served upon the defendants. Consequently, they could not contest the suit by filing written statement and leading evidences. Resultantly, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 2-3-2015 in preliminary form and thereafter an Advocate Commissioner was appointed for effecting partition physically who without visiting the suit property and letting know the fact to the defendants submitted a report before the trial court. 

4. The trial court in the absence of any objection against the report accepted the same and made the preliminary decree final on 24-2-2016. Thereafter, the decree holder opposite party No. 1 put the decree in execution by filing Title Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 on 09-6-2016. The petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 05 of 2017 on 16-5-2017 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree. In the said case the plaintiff opposite party appeared and filed written objection, before filing of the said miscellaneous case the present petitioner along with others, instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 on 23-3-2017, challenging the preliminary decree signed on 08-3-2016 passed in Partition Suit No. 32 of 2011. 

5. By this time, execution case was proceeding in accordance with law and for effecting delivery of possession, the court deployed police force with District Nazir and appointed Advocate Commissioner and issued writ of delivery of possession by order No. 13 dated 13-3-2017. Pursuant to writ of delivery of possession Advocate Commissioner and Nazir of the court submitted their report on 27-3-2017 along with bill, praying for withdrawing the same. In the meantime, plaintiff of Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 filed an application on 23-3-2017 praying for stay further proceeding of the Execution Case No. 04 of 2017. 

6. The trial court heard the application and upon hearing by its order dated 1-6-2017 allowed the application and stayed proceedings in Title Execution Suit No. 04 of 2016 and also by the said order rejected the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the trial court, passed in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017, the opposite party No. 1 preferred Civil Revision No. 32 of 2017 before the District Judge, Barguna who upon hearing by the impugned judgment and order dated 28-2-2018 allowed the revision and set-aside the order of the trial court, directing Advocate Commissioner to submit report afresh by investigating physically. At this juncture, the petitioner moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking leave to revision and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

8. Mr Md Sagir Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that in the event of filing a suit by the judgment debtor against whom decree was passed, challenging the decree, the court ought to have stayed the proceeding of execution case till disposal of the suit. Accordingly, the trial court rightly allowed the application and stayed further proceeding of the execution case by order dated 1-6-2017, but the revisional court while allowing the revision and setting aside the order of the trial court did not even given a single finding why the execution proceeding should not be stayed but the revisional court only decided the matter in respect of rejection of Advocate Commissioner's report, thus, the judgment and order of the revisional court below suffers from legal insufficiency, as such, the same is liable to be set-aside. In support of his submissions he has referred to the cases of Zagir Hussain vs Aminul Hague and others reported in 1999 BLD (HCD) 366 = 51 DLR 425 and Narsidas Nathubhai Vohra vs Manharsingh Agarsing Thakor reported in AIR 1931 Bombay 247. 

9. Mr Hasan Tareq, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1 submits that after passing preliminary decree the suit property was physically partitioned by an Advocate Commissioner who submitted an exhaustive report, wherein the petitioner himself put his hand as one of the witnesses. Therefore, it was very much within their knowledge that a decree has been passed by the court giving saham to the plaintiff in Partition Suit No. 32 of 2011. 

10. He further submits that the petitioner along with others filed Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 32 of 2011 and after filing of the suit they also filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 05 of 2017 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code on 16-5-2017. When the opposite party No. 1 filed written objection in the case they did not proceed with the same, consequently, the case was dismissed for default on 24-4-2018. 

11. The petitioner knowing fully well about the decree allowed to proceed the Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 upto delivery of possession. When delivery of possession was made and report has been submitted before the executing court to that effect, the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 filed an application praying for stay further proceedings of the Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 wherein no further action was required to be taken. After delivery of possession only thing left with the court to accept the report and to pass an order disposing the execution case with full satisfaction, as such, there is nothing to be stayed by the court below. Hence the revisional court rightly set-aside the order of the trial court. 

12. Heard the learned Advocates of both the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017, order sheet in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, application for stay, impugned judgment and order of both the courts below. 

13. From annexue-Al it appears that Partition Suit No. 32 of 2011 was decreed ex-parte on 2-3-2015 and decree was drawn on 8-3-2015. Thereafter, for effecting partition physically, an Advocate Commissioner was appointed who submitted a report with a sketch map effecting partition of the suit property. Then, the preliminary decree was made final on 24-2-2016 by accepting and making the report of the commissioner part of the decree. Thereafter, the decree was put in execution by filing Title Execution Case No. 04 of 2016. The petitioner along with others instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 as well as filed Miscellaneous Case No. 05 of 2017 under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code praying for setting aside the ex-parte decree. Subsequently, the petitioners allowed to dismiss the case for default on 24-4-2018. The petitioner, as plaintiff, in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 filed an application before the trial court on 23-3-2017 praying for stay further proceedings of Execution Case No 04 of 2016. The opposite party No. 1, as defendant, contested the application and the trial court upon hearing allowed the application and stayed further proceeding of the execution case. But the trial court while staying the proceeding in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, unfortunately and wrongly rejected the commission report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, which it cannot do legally. Because in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 no report was filed by the Advocate Commissioner but it was submitted in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 and the court can accept or reject the same by passing an order in the execution proceeding, not in any other suit or case. 

14. The defendant opposite party No. 1 challenged the order of the trial court by filing Civil Revision No. 32 of 2017 before the District Judge, who by the impugned judgment and order dated 28-2-2018 allowed the revision and set-aside the order dated 1-6-2017 passed by the trial court in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 and directed further investigation of the property and to file a fresh report. 

15. From perusal of impugned order passed by the revisional court, it appears that unfortunately the revisional court failed to appreciate the fact that the commissioner report was submitted by the Advocate Commissioner in Title Execution Case No. 04 of 2016 not in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 and the trial court has had no scope or reason to accept or reject the commission report in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017. The revisional court also validated the order of the trial court and directed for further investigation and to submit a fresh report which the revisional court also cannot do. The order of the trial court connects two things, one is; rejection of commission report and another is order of stay staying proceeding in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016. But the revisional court only considered Advocate Commissioner report without applying judicial mind and did not even a single word or finding given in respect of stay further proceeding of the Execution Case No. 04 of 2016. The impugned order as a whole seems to be unjust and impracticable. 

16. As apprised by Mr Hasan Tareq, learned Advocate for the opposite party, the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner is relating to delivery of possession and for withdrawal of commission fee and the said report in no way touches the merit of the preliminary decree or measurement and distribution of property by filed book or sketch-map and there was nothing contrary to the decree of the trial court. As such, there was no earthly reason to reject that report which only said that they effected physical possession with police force and District Nazir. However, this matter is not at all concerned in this revision, as no revision preferred by the decree holder against the rejection of Advocate Commissioner's report. 

17. Now the question before this court, whether in the event of challenging a decree by filing an independent suit by the judgment debtor, execution proceeding can be stayed till disposal of the suit. To appreciate the matter, I have gone through the relevant provisions contain in Order 21, rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Said provision of law provides that an application for stay of execution case is maintainable in the subsequent suit filed by the judgment debtor challenging the decree passed in earlier suit and arising out of the decree between the decree holder and the judgment debtor. In the instant case it appears that the Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 has been filed challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 32 of 2011 in preliminary form. But not against the final decree and in the suit, the plaintiff filed application praying for stay further proceeding of Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, wherein record shows that possession of the property already delivered but in the order sheet of Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, this Court finds nothing to the effect that in execution of the decree possession of the property has been delivered to the decree holder as yet. 

18. Both the parties could not apprise the court actual fact and position of the execution case, but from last order dated 8-6-2017 passed in Execution Case No. 04 of 2016, it appears that the proceedings of the case has been stayed by the court in Title Suit No. 31 of 2017. 

19. In this situation, I find that admittedly, a suit is pending before the court challenging the decree under execution and the execution proceedings has not yet been ended with full satisfaction, meaning thereby, it is still pending. For ensuring justice and to prevent various proceedings, I think that the proper course is to stay further proceeding of the execution case till disposal of the suit. It is to be mentioned that the plaintiff did not file the suit challenging the final decree which is under execution and the plaintiff could not confirm whether possession of the property already delivered to the decree holder in Title Suit No. 32 of 2011. In the event of delivery of possession to the decree holder the present Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 filed by the plaintiff would be incompetent for want of consequential relief in the form of recovery of possession. 

20. Since this matter is relating to an order of stay only, this Court refrained itself from making any observations regarding maintainability of the suit. 

21. Learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 1 submits that in the event of staying proceeding of execution case the possession delivered through court to the opposite party would be threatened by the plaintiff in suit. Considering such submissions, this court thinks that purpose of the parties will be served and justice will be met if the parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of the suit property. 

22. Taking into consideration the above, I find merit in the Rule. 

23. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however without any order as to costs. 

24. The impugned judgment and order dated 28-2-2018 passed in Civil Revision No. 42 of 2018 is hereby set-aside and the order dated 1-6-2017 passed by the trial court is hereby restored only to the extent of stay. 

25. Both the parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of possession of the suit property till disposal of Title Suit No. 31 of 2017. 

26. The trial court is hereby directed to dispose of the Title Suit No. 31 of 2017 within 06 (six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order positively. 

27. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. 

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned. 

End.
